sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasrāṇi patanti vyomni; tathā aśītiṃ parivatsarāṇi tān vai tudanti prapatataḥ prapātaṃ; bhīmā bhaumā rākṣasās tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāḥ
english: Sixty thousand years they fall through the sky, and then eighty more years besides; as they plummet headlong in their fall, terrible earthbound rākṣasas with sharp fangs torment them.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca yad enasas te patatas tudanti; bhīmā bhaumā rākṣasās tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāḥ kathaṃ bhavanti katham ābhavanti; kathaṃbhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti
english: Aṣṭaka said: When those terrible earthbound rākṣasas with sharp fangs torment the falling sinners, how do they come into being, how do they come to exist — in what manner do they become embryonic beings?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca asraṃ retaḥ puṣpaphalānupṛktam; anveti tad vai puruṣeṇa sṛṣṭam sa vai tasyā raja āpadyate vai; sa garbhabhūtaḥ samupaiti tatra
english: Yayāti said: Blood, seed, and the essence of flowers and fruits — that which is emitted by the man follows along; that indeed enters the woman's menstrual blood, and becoming an embryo it arrives there.

sanskrit: vanaspatīṃś cauṣadhīś cāviśanti; apo vāyuṃ pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣam catuṣpadaṃ dvipadaṃ cāpi sarvam; evaṃbhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti
english: They enter into trees and medicinal plants, into water, wind, earth, and the atmosphere, into all four-footed creatures and two-footed beings as well — in this manner do they become embryonic beings.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca anyad vapur vidadhātīha garbha; utāho svit svena kāmena yāti āpadyamāno narayonim etām; ācakṣva me saṃśayāt prabravīmi
english: Aṣṭaka said: Does the embryo fashion a different body here, or does it go of its own will when entering this human womb? Explain this to me — I speak from doubt.

sanskrit: śarīradehādisamucchrayaṃ ca; cakṣuḥśrotre labhate kena saṃjñām etat tattvaṃ sarvam ācakṣva pṛṣṭaḥ; kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tāta manyāma sarve
english: And how does the body with its form arise, and by what means does it gain awareness through eye and ear? Tell me all this truth when questioned — for we all regard you, dear one, as one who knows the field.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca vāyuḥ samutkarṣati garbhayonim; ṛtau retaḥ puṣparasānupṛktam sa tatra tanmātrakṛtādhikāraḥ; krameṇa saṃvardhayatīha garbham
english: Yayāti said: The wind draws up the embryonic matrix; in the fertile season it is mingled with the essence of seed and flower. There, holding sway through the subtle elements, it gradually nourishes and develops the embryo here.

sanskrit: sa jāyamāno vigṛhītagātraḥ; ṣaḍjñānaniṣṭhāyatano manuṣyaḥ sa śrotrābhyāṃ vedayatīha śabdaṃ; sarvaṃ rūpaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā ca
english: As it is born with its limbs fully formed, the human being is grounded in six modes of cognition; by means of the ears it perceives sound here, and sees all form through the eyes.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena gandhaṃ jihvayātho rasaṃ ca; tvacā sparśaṃ manasā veda bhāvam ity aṣṭakehopacitiṃ ca viddhi; mahātmanaḥ prāṇabhṛtaḥ śarīre
english: By the nose it smells fragrance, by the tongue it tastes flavour, by the skin it knows touch, and by the mind it knows inner states — so know, O Aṣṭaka, the accumulation of senses in the body of the great-souled living being.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca yaḥ saṃsthitaḥ puruṣo dahyate vā; nikhanyate vāpi nighṛṣyate vā abhāvabhūtaḥ sa vināśam etya; kenātmānaṃ cetayate purastāt
english: Aṣṭaka said: When a man has died and is burned, or is buried, or is ground to dust — having passed into non-being and reached destruction, by what means does the self become conscious again hereafter?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca hitvā so 'sūn suptavan niṣṭanitvā; purodhāya sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca anyāṃ yoniṃ pavanāgrānusārī; hitvā dehaṃ bhajate rājasiṃha
english: Yayāti said: Having abandoned the vital breaths like one falling asleep, having groaned, having placed merit and demerit before it, it follows at the tip of the wind, O lion among kings, and having left the body it enters another womb.

sanskrit: puṇyāṃ yoniṃ puṇyakṛto vrajanti; pāpāṃ yoniṃ pāpakṛto vrajanti kīṭāḥ pataṃgāś ca bhavanti pāpā; na me vivakṣāsti mahānubhāva
english: Those who have done good go to an auspicious womb; those who have done evil go to an evil womb — the wicked become insects and moths. I have no desire to say more, O great one.

sanskrit: catuṣpadā dvipadāḥ ṣaṭpadāś ca; tathābhūtā garbhabhūtā bhavanti ākhyātam etan nikhilena sarvaṃ; bhūyas tu kiṃ pṛcchasi rājasiṃha
english: Four-footed creatures, two-footed beings, and six-legged insects — in this way do they become embryonic forms. All this has been told to you in full; what more do you ask, O lion among kings?

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kiṃ svit kṛtvā labhate tāta lokān; martyaḥ śreṣṭhāṃs tapasā vidyayā vā tan me pṛṣṭaḥ śaṃsa sarvaṃ yathāvac; chubhāṃl lokān yena gacchet krameṇa
english: Aṣṭaka said: By doing what, dear one, does a mortal attain the highest worlds — by asceticism or by knowledge? Being asked, tell me all this truthfully, by what means one may reach the auspicious worlds in due order.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca tapaś ca dānaṃ ca śamo damaś ca; hrīr ārjavaṃ sarvabhūtānukampā naśyanti mānena tamo 'bhibhūtāḥ; puṃsaḥ sadaiveti vadanti santaḥ
english: Yayāti said: Asceticism, charity, tranquillity of mind, self-restraint, modesty, uprightness, and compassion toward all beings — these always perish in a man when overcome by darkness through arrogance; so say the good.

sanskrit: adhīyānaḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamāno; yo vidyayā hanti yaśaḥ pareṣām tasyāntavantaś ca bhavanti lokā; na cāsya tad brahma phalaṃ dadāti
english: He who studies and fancies himself a scholar yet destroys the reputation of others through his learning — his worlds come to an end, and that sacred knowledge bears no fruit for him.

sanskrit: catvāri karmāṇy abhayaṃkarāṇi; bhayaṃ prayacchanty ayathākṛtāni mānāgnihotram uta mānamaunaṃ; mānenādhītam uta mānayajñaḥ
english: Four acts that should bring fearlessness bring fear instead when performed with arrogance: the agnihotra performed with arrogance, silence practiced with arrogance, learning undertaken with arrogance, and the sacrifice offered with arrogance.

sanskrit: na mānyamāno mudam ādadīta; na saṃtāpaṃ prāpnuyāc cāvamānāt santaḥ sataḥ pūjayantīha loke; nāsādhavaḥ sādhubuddhiṃ labhante
english: One should not take joy when honoured, nor grieve when dishonoured; the good honour the good in this world — the wicked never attain the insight of the virtuous.

sanskrit: iti dadyād iti yajed ity adhīyīta me vratam ity asminn abhayāny āhus tāni varjyāni nityaśaḥ
english: "Thus shall I give, thus shall I sacrifice, thus shall I study — this is my vow": in such attitude they speak of fearless deeds, yet these very things are to be avoided always when done from egotism.

sanskrit: yenāśrayaṃ vedayante purāṇaṃ; manīṣiṇo mānasamānabhaktam tan niḥśreyas taijasaṃ rūpam etya; parāṃ śāntiṃ prāpnuyuḥ pretya ceha
english: Through that ancient refuge which the wise, devoted equally to honour and dishonour, come to know — attaining that supreme luminous form of the highest good, they reach perfect peace, both here and after death.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca caran gṛhasthaḥ katham eti devān; kathaṃ bhikṣuḥ katham ācāryakarmā vānaprasthaḥ satpathe saṃniviṣṭo; bahūny asmin saṃprati vedayanti
english: Aṣṭaka said: How does the householder, pursuing his duties, reach the gods? How does the mendicant? How does the teacher's pupil? And the forest-dweller established on the good path? Many things are now known about this.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca āhūtādhyāyī gurukarmasvacodyaḥ; pūrvotthāyī caramaṃ copaśāyī mṛdur dānto dhṛtimān apramattaḥ; svādhyāyaśīlaḥ sidhyati brahmacārī
english: Yayāti said: He who studies when called upon, who is diligent in the teacher's work without being prompted, who rises first and retires last, who is gentle, restrained, steadfast, and heedful, and devoted to personal study — such a brahmacharī attains success.

sanskrit: dharmāgataṃ prāpya dhanaṃ yajeta; dadyāt sadaivātithīn bhojayec ca anādadānaś ca parair adattaṃ; saiṣā gṛhasthopaniṣat purāṇī
english: Having acquired wealth obtained by righteous means, one should sacrifice, give freely, and always feed guests; and one should not take what has not been given by others — this is the ancient secret teaching of the householder.

sanskrit: svavīryajīvī vṛjinān nivṛtto; dātā parebhyo na paropatāpī tādṛṅ muniḥ siddhim upaiti mukhyāṃ; vasann araṇye niyatāhāraceṣṭaḥ
english: He who lives by his own exertion, who has turned away from sin, who gives to others without tormenting any being — such a sage, dwelling in the forest with regulated food and conduct, attains the highest success.

sanskrit: aśilpajīvī nagṛhaś ca nityaṃ; jitendriyaḥ sarvato vipramuktaḥ anokasārī laghur alpacāraś; caran deśān ekacaraḥ sa bhikṣuḥ
english: He who lives without a craft, perpetually without a home, with senses conquered, wholly freed from all bonds, who moves from one resting place to another, light and of few wants, wandering through lands alone — he is the true mendicant.

sanskrit: rātryā yayā cābhijitāś ca lokā; bhavanti kāmā vijitāḥ sukhāś ca tām eva rātriṃ prayateta vidvān; araṇyasaṃstho bhavituṃ yatātmā
english: The night by which the worlds are won, by which desires are conquered and joys obtained — that very night the wise man, with a disciplined self, should strive to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: daśaiva pūrvān daśa cāparāṃs tu; jñātīn sahātmānam athaikaviṃśam araṇyavāsī sukṛte dadhāti; vimucyāraṇye svaśarīradhātūn
english: Ten ancestors before him, ten relatives after, and himself as the twenty-first — the forest-dweller places them all in the realm of good deeds, releasing the constituent elements of his own body in the forest.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kati svid eva munayo maunāni kati cāpy uta bhavantīti tad ācakṣva śrotum icchāmahe vayam
english: Aṣṭaka said: How many kinds of sages are there, and how many kinds of silence are there? Tell us this — we wish to hear.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca araṇye vasato yasya grāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ grāme vā vasato 'raṇyaṃ sa muniḥ syāj janādhipa
english: Yayāti said: He for whom the village lies behind while dwelling in the forest, or for whom the forest lies behind while dwelling in the village — that man may be called a sage, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kathaṃ svid vasato 'raṇye grāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ grāme vā vasato 'raṇyaṃ kathaṃ bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Aṣṭaka said: How is it that when one dwells in the forest the village comes to lie behind, and how is it that when dwelling in the village the forest comes to lie behind?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca na grāmyam upayuñjīta ya āraṇyo munir bhavet tathāsya vasato 'raṇye grāmo bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Yayāti said: He who would be a forest-dwelling sage should not make use of village things; in that way, even while dwelling in the forest, the village comes to lie behind him.

sanskrit: anagnir aniketaś ca agotracaraṇo muniḥ kaupīnācchādanaṃ yāvat tāvad icchec ca cīvaram
english: Without fire, without a fixed dwelling, moving without clan affiliations, the sage should desire clothing only to the extent of a loincloth for covering.

sanskrit: yāvat prāṇābhisaṃdhānaṃ tāvad icchec ca bhojanam tathāsya vasato grāme 'raṇyaṃ bhavati pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: He should desire food only to the extent of sustaining the vital breaths — in that way, even while dwelling in the village, the forest comes to lie behind him.

sanskrit: yas tu kāmān parityajya tyaktakarmā jitendriyaḥ ātiṣṭheta munir maunaṃ sa loke siddhim āpnuyāt
english: But the sage who abandons desires, who has given up action, whose senses are conquered, and who abides in silence — he attains perfection in this world.

sanskrit: dhautadantaṃ kṛttanakhaṃ sadā snātam alaṃkṛtam asitaṃ sitakarmasthaṃ kas taṃ nārcitum arhati
english: With teeth washed, nails trimmed, always bathed and adorned, dark in complexion yet established in pure deeds — who would not be worthy to worship such a one?

sanskrit: tapasā karśitaḥ kṣāmaḥ kṣīṇamāṃsāsthiśoṇitaḥ yadā bhavati nirdvandvo munir maunaṃ samāsthitaḥ atha lokam imaṃ jitvā lokaṃ vijayate param
english: Emaciated by austerity, lean, with flesh, bone, and blood wasted away — when the sage becomes free from the pairs of opposites and abides in silence, then, having conquered this world, he conquers the world beyond.

sanskrit: āsyena tu yadāhāraṃ govan mṛgayate muniḥ athāsya lokaḥ pūrvo yaḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: When the sage seeks his food with his mouth alone like a cow, then whatever was his former world becomes fit for immortality.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kataras tv etayoḥ pūrvaṃ devānām eti sātmyatām ubhayor dhāvato rājan sūryācandramasor iva
english: Aṣṭaka said: Which of these two first attains oneness with the gods, as they both race, O king, like the sun and the moon?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca aniketo gṛhastheṣu kāmavṛtteṣu saṃyataḥ grāma eva vasan bhikṣus tayoḥ pūrvataraṃ gataḥ
english: Yayāti said: The mendicant who is without a fixed home, who is restrained amid householders given over to desire, who dwells in the very village — he of the two has gone ahead.

sanskrit: aprāpya dīrgham āyus tu yaḥ prāpto vikṛtiṃ caret tapyeta yadi tat kṛtvā caret so 'nyat tatas tapaḥ
english: He who has not attained a long life and yet has met with adversity should practise austerity; if he has done that and practises it, let him then proceed to other austerities beyond that.

sanskrit: yad vai nṛśaṃsaṃ tad apathyam āhur; yaḥ sevate dharmam anarthabuddhiḥ asvo 'py anīśaś ca tathaiva rājaṃs; tadārjavaṃ sa samādhis tadāryam
english: What is cruel they call harmful; he who practises dharma with a mind set on what is not right — even he is without true self-mastery, O king; that uprightness is his concentration, that his nobility.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kenāsi dūtaḥ prahito 'dya rājan; yuvā sragvī darśanīyaḥ suvarcāḥ kuta āgataḥ katarasyāṃ diśi tvam; utāho svit pārthivaṃ sthānam asti
english: Aṣṭaka said: By whom were you sent as a messenger today, O king — young, garlanded, handsome, radiant? From where have you come, and in which direction are you? Or do you have a royal station?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca imaṃ bhaumaṃ narakaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyaḥ; praveṣṭum urvīṃ gaganād viprakīrṇaḥ uktvāhaṃ vaḥ prapatiṣyāmy anantaraṃ; tvaranti māṃ brāhmaṇā lokapālāḥ
english: Yayāti said: My merit exhausted, I have been scattered from the sky to enter this earthly hell; having spoken to you, I shall fall at once — the brahmins and the world-guardians urge me on.

sanskrit: satāṃ sakāśe tu vṛtaḥ prapātas; te saṃgatā guṇavantaś ca sarve śakrāc ca labdho hi varo mayaiṣa; patiṣyatā bhūmitale narendra
english: My fall has been chosen in the presence of the good — they are all assembled here and endowed with virtue. This boon was obtained by me even from Indra — that I should fall upon the earth, O lord of men.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ mā prapata prapātaṃ; yadi lokāḥ pārthiva santi me 'tra yady antarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāḥ; kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye
english: Aṣṭaka said: I ask you — do not fall in your fall; if there are worlds belonging to me here, whether stationed in the atmosphere or in the sky, take them — I regard you as one who knows the field of dharma.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yāvat pṛthivyāṃ vihitaṃ gavāśvaṃ; sahāraṇyaiḥ paśubhiḥ parvataiś ca tāval lokā divi te saṃsthitā vai; tathā vijānīhi narendrasiṃha
english: Yayāti said: As many as the cows and horses distributed over the earth, along with the forest animals and mountains — that many worlds of yours are established in the sky. Know it thus, O lion among lords of men.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca tāṃs te dadāmi mā prapata prapātaṃ; ye me lokā divi rājendra santi yady antarikṣe yadi vā divi śritās; tān ākrama kṣipram amitrasāha
english: Aṣṭaka said: I give you those worlds of mine — do not fall in your fall; whatever worlds of mine exist in the sky, whether stationed in the atmosphere or established in the heavens, mount them quickly, O destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca nāsmadvidho 'brāhmaṇo brahmavic ca; pratigrahe vartate rājamukhya yathā pradeyaṃ satataṃ dvijebhyas; tathādadaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ narendra
english: Yayāti said: One like me who is not a brahmin, even if learned in the Vedas, does not engage in receiving gifts, O foremost among kings; as what should constantly be given to the twice-born, so did I formerly give, O lord of men.

sanskrit: nābrāhmaṇaḥ kṛpaṇo jātu jīved; yā cāpi syād brāhmaṇī vīrapatnī so 'haṃ yadaivākṛtapūrvaṃ careyaṃ; vivitsamānaḥ kim u tatra sādhu
english: A non-brahmin should never live a wretched life depending on others; likewise a brahmin woman who is the wife of a hero — I am such a one; what good would it be if I were to do what was never done before, when seeking to know the truth?

sanskrit: pratardana uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ spṛhaṇīyarūpa; pratardano 'haṃ yadi me santi lokāḥ yady antarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāḥ; kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye
english: Pratardana said: I ask you, O one of desirable form — I am Pratardana; if there are worlds belonging to me, whether stationed in the atmosphere or established in the sky, I offer them; I regard you as one who knows the field of dharma.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca santi lokā bahavas te narendra; apy ekaikaḥ sapta saptāpy ahāni madhucyuto ghṛtapṛktā viśokās; te nāntavantaḥ pratipālayanti
english: Yayāti said: Many worlds are yours, O lord of men; even individually they are seven times seven days each — dripping with honey, mixed with clarified butter, free from grief; those boundless worlds await you.

sanskrit: pratardana uvāca tāṃs te dadāmi mā prapata prapātaṃ; ye me lokās tava te vai bhavantu yady antarikṣe yadi vā divi śritās; tān ākrama kṣipram apetamohaḥ
english: Pratardana said: I give you those worlds — do not fall in your fall; whatever worlds are mine, let them truly be yours; whether stationed in the atmosphere or established in the sky, mount them quickly, O one freed from delusion.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca na tulyatejāḥ sukṛtaṃ kāmayeta; yogakṣemaṃ pārthiva pārthivaḥ san daivādeśād āpadaṃ prāpya vidvāṃś; caren nṛśaṃsaṃ na hi jātu rājā
english: Yayāti said: One of equal splendour should not desire another's merits; being a king, O king, and meeting with adversity by the decree of fate, the wise man should not act cruelly — for a king should never do so.

sanskrit: dharmyaṃ mārgaṃ cetayāno yaśasyaṃ; kuryān nṛpo dharmam avekṣamāṇaḥ na madvidho dharmabuddhiḥ prajānan; kuryād evaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ māṃ yathāttha
english: Contemplating the path of righteousness and honour, a king should act with regard to dharma; one like me, who knows dharma in mind, knowing it, should not act so wretchedly as you describe.

sanskrit: kuryām apūrvaṃ na kṛtaṃ yad anyair; vivitsamānaḥ kim u tatra sādhu bruvāṇam evaṃ nṛpatiṃ yayātiṃ; nṛpottamo vasumanābravīt tam
english: I should do what is unprecedented, not done by others — what good is there in that when one is seeking to know the truth? As king Yayāti spoke thus, the most eminent of kings, Vasumanā, addressed him.

sanskrit: vasumanā uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vasumanā rauśadaśvir; yady asti loko divi mahyaṃ narendra yady antarikṣe prathito mahātman; kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye
english: Vasumanā said: I ask you — I am Vasumanā, son of Rauśadaśva; if there is a world in the sky for me, O lord of men, whether spread through the atmosphere, O great-souled one, I offer it; I regard you as one who knows the field of dharma.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yad antarikṣaṃ pṛthivī diśaś ca; yat tejasā tapate bhānumāṃś ca lokās tāvanto divi saṃsthitā vai; te nāntavantaḥ pratipālayanti
english: Yayāti said: What the atmosphere, the earth, the directions, and the radiant sun illuminates with its brilliance — that many worlds are established in the sky for you; those boundless worlds await you.

sanskrit: vasumanā uvāca tāṃs te dadāmi pata mā prapātaṃ; ye me lokās tava te vai bhavantu krīṇīṣvaināṃs tṛṇakenāpi rājan; pratigrahas te yadi samyak praduṣṭaḥ
english: Vasumanā said: I give you those worlds — do not fall in your fall; whatever worlds are mine, let them truly be yours; buy them even for a blade of grass, O king — if the act of receiving a gift is truly corrupted for you.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca na mithyāhaṃ vikrayaṃ vai smarāmi; vṛthā gṛhītaṃ śiśukāc chaṅkamānaḥ kuryāṃ na caivākṛtapūrvam anyair; vivitsamānaḥ kim u tatra sādhu
english: Yayāti said: I do not recall having made a false sale; I would not doubtfully take something obtained in vain from a child, nor would I do what was never done by others — what good is there in that when seeking to know?

sanskrit: vasumanā uvāca tāṃs tvaṃ lokān pratipadyasva rājan; mayā dattān yadi neṣṭaḥ krayas te ahaṃ na tān vai pratigantā narendra; sarve lokās tava te vai bhavantu
english: Vasumanā said: Accept those worlds, O king, given by me; if the purchase is not to your liking, I shall not take them back, O lord of men — let all those worlds truly be yours.

sanskrit: śibir uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ śibir auśīnaro 'haṃ; mamāpi lokā yadi santīha tāta yady antarikṣe yadi vā divi śritāḥ; kṣetrajñaṃ tvāṃ tasya dharmasya manye
english: Śibi said: I ask you — I am Śibi, son of Uśīnara; if there are worlds for me here as well, dear one, whether in the atmosphere or established in the sky, I offer them — I regard you as one who knows the field of dharma.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca na tvaṃ vācā hṛdayenāpi vidvan; parīpsamānān nāvamaṃsthā narendra tenānantā divi lokāḥ śritās te; vidyudrūpāḥ svanavanto mahāntaḥ
english: Yayāti said: You, O wise one, have never slighted with word or even with heart those who sought your protection, O lord of men; therefore boundless worlds are established in the sky for you — vast, radiant as lightning, resonant with sound.

sanskrit: śibir uvāca tāṃs tvaṃ lokān pratipadyasva rājan; mayā dattān yadi neṣṭaḥ krayas te na cāhaṃ tān pratipatsyeha dattvā; yatra gatvā tvam upāsse ha lokān
english: Śibi said: Accept those worlds, O king, given by me; if the purchase is not to your liking, I shall not take them back now having given them — go to those worlds which you worship, and dwell there.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yathā tvam indrapratimaprabhāvas; te cāpy anantā naradeva lokāḥ tathādya loke na rame 'nyadatte; tasmāc chibe nābhinandāmi dāyam
english: Yayāti said: As you are equal in splendour to Indra, so too are your worlds boundless, O lord of men; yet I take no pleasure today in what has been given by another; therefore, O Śibi, I do not rejoice in the gift.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca na ced ekaikaśo rājaṃl lokān naḥ pratinandasi sarve pradāya bhavate gantāro narakaṃ vayam
english: Aṣṭaka said: If you do not accept our worlds one by one, O king, then we shall all go to hell by giving them to you.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yad arhāya dadadhvaṃ tat santaḥ satyānṛśaṃsyataḥ ahaṃ tu nābhidhṛṣṭomi yatkṛtaṃ na mayā purā
english: Yayāti said: Give what is worthy to one who is worthy — you who are good, by the virtue of truth and non-cruelty; but I do not dare to do what was never done by me before.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca kasyaite pratidṛśyante rathāḥ pañca hiraṇmayāḥ uccaiḥ santaḥ prakāśante jvalanto 'gniśikhā iva
english: Aṣṭaka said: Whose are these five golden chariots that appear before us, standing high, gleaming, blazing like the flame of fire?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yuṣmān ete hi vakṣyanti rathāḥ pañca hiraṇmayāḥ uccaiḥ santaḥ prakāśante jvalanto 'gniśikhā iva
english: Yayāti said: These five golden chariots will carry you — standing high, gleaming, blazing like the flame of fire.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca ātiṣṭhasva rathaṃ rājan vikramasva vihāyasā vayam apy anuyāsyāmo yadā kālo bhaviṣyati
english: Aṣṭaka said: Mount the chariot, O king, stride forth through the sky; we too will follow when the time comes.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca sarvair idānīṃ gantavyaṃ sahasvargajito vayam eṣa no virajāḥ panthā dṛśyate devasadmanaḥ
english: Yayāti said: Now all must go together — we who have won heaven; this pure, unsullied path to the abode of the gods lies visible before us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te 'dhiruhya rathān sarve prayātā nṛpasattamāḥ ākramanto divaṃ bhābhir dharmeṇāvṛtya rodasī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: They all mounted the chariots and set forth, those most excellent of kings, ascending to heaven with their radiance, filling both heaven and earth with their dharma.

sanskrit: aṣṭaka uvāca ahaṃ manye pūrvam eko 'smi gantā; sakhā cendraḥ sarvathā me mahātmā kasmād evaṃ śibir auśīnaro 'yam; eko 'tyagāt sarvavegena vāhān
english: Aṣṭaka said: I think I alone am going ahead — and Indra is my great-souled friend in every way; but why has this Śibi, son of Uśīnara, alone surpassed all others with full speed in his vehicle?

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca adadād devayānāya yāvad vittam avindata uśīnarasya putro 'yaṃ tasmāc chreṣṭho hi naḥ śibiḥ
english: Yayāti said: This son of Uśīnara gave to the divine path all the wealth he possessed; therefore Śibi is indeed the best among us.

sanskrit: dānaṃ tapaḥ satyam athāpi dharmo; hrīḥ śrīḥ kṣamā saumya tathā titikṣā rājann etāny apratimasya rājñaḥ; śibeḥ sthitāny anṛśaṃsasya buddhyā evaṃvṛtto hrīniṣedhaś ca yasmāt; tasmāc chibir atyagād vai rathena
english: Charity, austerity, truth, dharma, modesty, fortune, forgiveness, O gentle one, and endurance — O king, these virtues of that matchless king, of Śibi of non-cruelty in mind, stand firm. And because he is of such conduct and restrained by modesty — therefore Śibi has indeed surpassed all in his chariot.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athāṣṭakaḥ punar evānvapṛcchan; mātāmahaṃ kautukād indrakalpam pṛcchāmi tvāṃ nṛpate brūhi satyaṃ; kutaś ca kasyāsi sutaś ca kasya kṛtaṃ tvayā yad dhi na tasya kartā; loke tvad anyaḥ kṣatriyo brāhmaṇo vā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Aṣṭaka questioned his maternal grandfather once more out of curiosity, that one equal to Indra: "I ask you, O king, tell me truly — from where are you, whose son are you, and whose are you? What you have done, no other doer of that deed exists — no other kṣatriya or brahmin in the world besides you."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yayātir asmi nahuṣasya putraḥ; pūroḥ pitā sārvabhaumas tv ihāsam guhyam arthaṃ māmakebhyo bravīmi; mātāmaho 'haṃ bhavatāṃ prakāśaḥ
english: Yayāti said: I am Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa; I was here as the universal emperor, father of Pūru; I tell you this hidden matter as my own — I am your maternal grandfather, now revealed to you.

sanskrit: sarvām imāṃ pṛthivīṃ nirjigāya; prasthe baddhvā hy adadaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ medhyān aśvān ekaśaphān surūpāṃs; tadā devāḥ puṇyabhājo bhavanti
english: I conquered all this earth and, having bound it as a package, I gave it to the brahmins; I gave consecrated horses, single-hoofed and well-formed; then the gods became sharers in the merit.

sanskrit: adām ahaṃ pṛthivīṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ; pūrṇām imām akhilāṃ vāhanasya gobhiḥ suvarṇena dhanaiś ca mukhyais; tatrāsan gāḥ śatam arbudāni
english: I gave the earth to the brahmins — this entire full earth — along with cattle as tribute, gold, and the finest riches; therein were ten billion cows.

sanskrit: satyena me dyauś ca vasuṃdharā ca; tathaivāgnir jvalate mānuṣeṣu na me vṛthā vyāhṛtam eva vākyaṃ; satyaṃ hi santaḥ pratipūjayanti sarve ca devā munayaś ca lokāḥ; satyena pūjyā iti me manogatam
english: By my truth, both the sky and the earth-bearing goddess stand firm, and fire blazes among human beings; not one word spoken by me has been in vain — for the good honour truth, as do all the gods, the sages, and the worlds; it is the thought of my mind that the worthy are honoured by truth.

sanskrit: yo naḥ svargajitaḥ sarvān yathāvṛttaṃ nivedayet anasūyur dvijāgrebhyaḥ sa labhen naḥ salokatām
english: Whoever, without envy, recounts to the foremost of the twice-born all of us who have won heaven, exactly as it happened — he shall attain the same world as ours.
